title: Calendar parser rejects explicit numeric dates
original_report: The Telegram bot asks for the date again when asked to add an event for 11.08 at 15:00.

candidates.candidate: Calendar parser supports only relative dates.
candidates.contract: A calendar command containing a valid day, month, and time should produce a calendar event.
candidates.trigger: Добавь в календарь на 11.08 15:00 посмотреть видео

expected: The parser returns 2026-08-11 15:00 in Europe/Kyiv for the supplied input.
actual: Before the fix, the parser returned None because it recognized only сегодня, завтра, and послезавтра.
reproduction: A focused pytest case calls MainOrchestrator._parse_calendar_datetime with a fixed clock and explicit numeric date.
failure_signal: The pre-fix assertion compared None with the expected Europe/Kyiv datetime and failed.
root_cause: The calendar date branch had no numeric day-month parser and returned None for 11.08.
fix_summary: Added numeric day-month parsing with optional year and support for colon, dot, and hyphen time separators; preserved relative-date parsing and cleaned date/time fragments from event titles.
why_causal: The new branch constructs the requested local datetime before the Google Calendar tool is called.

reproduction_files.summary: Regression coverage for explicit numeric date and time formats.

fix_files.summary: Calendar datetime parser and event-title cleanup.

limitations: This change covers numeric dates; weekday names such as во вторник remain outside the approved fix scope.
Google OAuth and Calendar API availability still depend on the bot's environment configuration.
residual_risks: An explicitly supplied date in the past with an explicit year is still rejected rather than silently moved to another year.
notes: No dependencies or public APIs changed.
